articles.title: Evenepoel wins fourth world time trial title in a row, Reusser retains her crown
articles.summary: Remco Evenepoel dominates men’s event in Montreal. Marlen Reusser denies Zoe Backstedt in women’s race. Remco Evenepoel etched his name into the history books with a dominant fourth successive men’s world time-trial victory in Montreal on Sunday.
body: The 2024 Olympic champion came into the race as the overwhelming favourite and he did not disappoint. Evenepoel was already more than 30 seconds ahead of the rest by the second intermediate time check, just over halfway along the 39.2km (24.4 mile) route.

By the time he reached the finish line, the 26-year-old Belgian had put almost a minute into second-placed Filippo Ganna of Italy, with the French rider Paul Seixas taking third another 15 seconds back. Evenepoel has not lost a time trial since the 2025 Tour de France.

Evenepoel becomes the first man to win the time trial world title four times in a row, while also equalling the record number of overall titles held by Germany’s Tony Martin and the Swiss rider Fabian Cancellara.

He has enjoyed his best season to date so far this year, winning the Amstel Gold Race, Clásica San Sebastián and Grand Prix de Québec, as well as finishing second behind Tadej Pogacar this year at the Tour de France.

articles.title: Carrick disputes Cunha’s claim that Manchester United lacked energy in Fulham draw
articles.summary: Michael Carrick insists team ‘kept pushing’ for leveller. Matheus Cunha: ‘Fulham put in more energy than us’ Michael Carrick rejected the suggestion that his Manchester United players lacked physical fitness after they snatched a last-gasp 1-1 draw at Fulham on Sunday.
body: United were poor after the restart at 0-0, leading up to a disastrous Lisandro Martínez own goal in the 63rd minute, with Cunha saying they had to give more. “In the beginning of the second half, Fulham put in more energy than us and we cannot accept this,” Cunha said.

The draw was not the result Carrick or United wanted after a week during which they lost the derby against Manchester City and exited the Carabao Cup against Brighton; both matches were at Old Trafford. Carrick will take it under the circum­stances and he tried to ­highlight the positives which he said took in the never-say-die spirit of his ­players. They fought until the end and were rewarded when ­Cunha’s shot from distance took a heavy deflection off the ­Fulham defender David ­Affengruber to wrongfoot Bernd Leno.

Carrick said he did not agree with Cunha’s comment about the collective energy levels. “I don’t, ­particularly,” the manager said. “The way we finished the game … it didn’t look like that for me. I was quite happy with the way we finished the game. We kept pushing. I don’t think that’s an issue, no.

articles.title: Smith wins World Series of Darts Finals as Littler run ends
articles.summary: England's Ross Smith shocks Wales' Gerwyn Price to win World Series of Darts Finals as Luke Littler's clean-sweep dream ends in last eight in Amsterdam.
body: Englishman Ross Smith won the final six legs to produce a shock 11-5 victory over two-time former winner Gerwyn Price in the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.
It was just a second major title for the 37-year-old, whose only previous success at this level of the PDC World Tour came at the European Championship in 2022.
But the world number 14 overpowered his loftier opponent with a barrage of 180s, hitting 11 maximums, compared to Welshman Price's five, to finish a deserved winner.
It was a fitting finale to a tournament of shocks that saw world champion Luke Littler lose in the quarter-finals and miss out on his quest to claim a clean sweep of the major PDC titles in 2026.

articles.title: Manchester United’s engine room runs out of steam as fans voice frustration | Jacob Steinberg
articles.summary: Carrick’s side were short on inspiration, despite the summer spend in midfield, and the lack of quality in the final third was stark. One of the more damning aspects of Manchester United’s tortured rebuild is their inability to multitask.
body: United remain a listless, drifting operation. The ownership is reviled and the fanbase is becoming increasingly mutinous. It was not just Gary Neville seeing red as he commentated on United’s dismal efforts away to winless Fulham. There was an ominous shift in the mood in the away end at Craven Cottage, summed up by the boos that greeted Michael Carrick substituting Kobbie Mainoo with 10 minutes to go.

Carrick filled in as an emergency centre-back when United last lost this fixture, way back in December 2009. This has been a happy hunting ground since then and there was a sense of inevitability to United saving themselves on Sunday, although that was more to do with Fulham’s nerves at 1-0 up than any great show of defiance from the visitors when a third defeat in the space of a week was on the cards.

articles.title: Elvira’s fairytale crumbles at the last to hand Spaun PGA Championship title
articles.summary: World No 294 lets victory slip in agonising fashion. JJ Spaun triumphs by two shots at Wentworth. We will come to JJ Spaun and Jeremy Clarkson later. Only those without an ounce of compassion in their body could feel no sympathy for Manuel Elvira.
body: What happened next was a form of sporting torture rather than the realisation of a fairytale. Elvira pulled his layup into a bunker, flew the green, fluffed a chip into another sand trap and missed a bogey putt from 4ft. He did exceptionally well not to burst into tears. The disastrous 18th meant Elvira finished in a four-way tie for second place. Even Spaun, a winner on his Wentworth debut, had to be bashful at the manner of success.

“It is devastating that I hit the wrong shot on the layup and left myself the toughest shot in the fairway bunker,” Elvira said. “I wasn’t able to pull it off. I have played some of the best golf probably of my life.”

Beware the jilted golfer. Spaun arrived in England carrying a grudge at being overlooked for next weekend’s Presidents Cup where the US will take on an international team at Medinah. His omission was odd even before this victory. Rory McIlroy, during post-tournament media duties, had assumed Spaun was part of Brandt Snedeker’s team. Americans have now won three of the last six editions of the DP World Tour’s flagship event.

articles.title: Elvira loses nerve as Spaun triumphs at Wentworth
articles.summary: Manuel Elvira choked back the tears as an elated JJ Spaun celebrated becoming only the third US player to win the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth.
body: The 2025 US Open champion joins Billy Horschel and the legendary Arnold Palmer on a storied list of winners that also includes Tony Jacklin, Sir Nick Faldo, Seve Ballesteros, Jose Maria Olazabal and Rory McIlroy.
However, it was hard not to feel sympathy for Elvira, the unknown 30-year-old from Santander.

Ranked 294th in the world, this had looked like being the moment he had longed for when he stepped on to the final tee with a first victory in his sights - straight off the back of outrageous eagle on the 17th.
Having twice made birdies on the friendly par five this week, a third was hardly implausible - while a par would have ensured a play-off with Spaun, already in the clubhouse at 17 under par.

articles.title: GB's Backstedt wins world time-trial silver
articles.summary: Britain's Zoe Backstedt, 21, wins silver in the women's time trial and Belgium's Remco Evenepoel claims a fourth men's title at the UCI World Road Championships in Montreal.
body: The 21-year-old Welsh rider could have opted to defend the under-23 title she won last year.

But instead she stepped up to elite level and finished 40.11 seconds behind defending champion Marlen Reusser of Switzerland, who retained her crown on her 35th birthday with a winning time of 50 minutes 24.44 seconds.
Belgium's Remco Evenpoel, meanwhile, became the first rider to win the men's time trial for a fourth consecutive occasion.
The 26-year-old reigning Olympic champion joins Germany's Tony Martin and Swiss rider Fabian Cancellara as the only men to have won the title four times.

articles.title: 49ers WR Demarcus Robinson carted off after suffering ankle injury early in matchup vs. Dolphins
articles.summary: AP Photo/Kelley L. Cox. The San Francisco 49ers may be down yet another wide receiver. The 49ers lost wideout Demarcus Robinson in the first half of their matchup with the Miami Dolphins on Sunday afternoon.
body: Robinson made it to the sidelines on his own, but he was carted off the field. The 49ers initially said he was questionable to return, but then ruled him out just after halftime.
Robinson had a team-high 35 yards on three catches when he went down. Quarterback Brock Purdy scrambled for a 2-yard touchdown just two plays later, which put them up 14-3 at the time.

Robinson had 50 yards and a touchdown on two catches in the team's 27-7 win over the Los Angeles Rams in Australia to open the season this fall. The 31-year-old is in the final year of a two-year deal with San Francisco.

While specifics of Robinson's injury aren't yet known, he's just the latest 49ers wide receiver dealing with an injury this fall. The team lost rookie De'Zhaun Stribling for around 10 weeks after he underwent surgery to repair the deltoid ligament sprain in his left ankle. Stribling went down in their opener against the Rams, too. The team already lost wide receiver Ricky Pearsall to a season-ending injury this offseason, and Christian Kirk is still working back from IR with a calf injury.

"Those were two clear red cards. Given the difficulties we faced afterwards playing 11 against 10, we can only imagine what 50 minutes of 11 against nine would have been like.

articles.title: Real Madrid substitute completed as many dribbles as Vinícius & Mbappé combined vs Atlético
articles.summary: A head-turning statistic surrounding the attacking output of Real Madrid trio Vinícius Jr, Kylian Mbappé and Yan Diomandé has come to the fore on Sunday evening. This of course comes after all three were on the losing side in the season’s first edition of the Madrid Derby.
body: Real Madrid made the short trip across Spain’s capital earlier today, to lock horns with bitter rivals Atlético. The aforementioned Vinícius Jr and Kylian Mbappé featured from the off in the fixture, as the visitors’ key attacking outlets.
En route to an eventual 2-1 defeat, however, both struggled to impact proceedings in a meaningful way, restricted to half-chances and shots from distance.

Blancos summer signing Yan Diomandé, meanwhile, was introduced off the bench during the 2nd-half in the derby. And despite José Mourinho’s troops having been a man down, the young Ivorian managed to beat out the respective dribbling tallies notched by his attacking partners-in-crime, in just over half an hour of play.
‘Yan Diomandé completed the same number of dribbles (4) in 36 minutes and with one player fewer than Mbappé (3) and Vinícius (1) combined in the ENTIRE match.’

articles.title: Middlesex beat Leicestershire Foxes to end 36-year List A trophy wait
articles.summary: Middlesex ended a 36-year List A trophy drought by beating Leicestershire Foxes by 31 runs to win the Metro Bank One Day Cup in a low-scoring final at Trent Bridge.
body: Ryan Higgins made a superb maiden List A hundred from 115 balls with Harry Duke (55) backing him up as their 135-run sixth-wicket partnership steered Middlesex from 71-5 to 231 all out after Foxes all-rounder Ian Holland took 5-36 and wicketkeeper Ben Cox held five catches. Higgins and Duke were making their first appearances for Middlesex in this year's competition.

New Zealand international batter Nick Kelly hit an equally brilliant 103 (107 balls) to lead a Leicestershire fightback from 79-5 but it was not enough to haul his side over the line, Tom Helm (3-32) claiming his vital wicket in a superb late spell as the Foxes were bowled out for 200.

In an impressive performance in the field by Middlesex, Toby Roland-Jones (3-27) showed his quality and 21-year-old pace prospect Naayva Sharma (3-37) finished as the competition's leading wicket-taker with 20.
Against a background of turmoil off the field, the win is a first for Middlesex in a List A final since they beat Derbyshire to lift the 1990 Refuge Assurance Cup.

articles.title: Smith thrashes Price to win World Series after Littler's shock exit
articles.summary: Ross Smith thrashed Gerwyn Price 11-5 to become World Series of Darts champion, while Luke Littler's hopes of a clean sweep of all major PDC titles in 2026 was dashed in the quarter-finals.
body: Smith won the last six legs, fired in 11 maximums, recorded back-to-back ton-plus finishes and went at 46 per cent on his doubles as he overwhelmed Price in Amsterdam on Sunday night to claim his second PDC major, after the 2022 European Championship.

Price, who missed a host of doubles in the back end of the match as his checkout percentage dropped to 26, has seven PDC majors in total, including three Grand Slams and the 2021 World Championship, but none since the World Series Finals in 2022.
Speaking bluntly afterwards on ITV4, the Welshman said: "I am playing some good darts, I am earning some good money. If I never win a major again I really don't care as long as I am doing well.

"I am gutted I've lost but if I never win another major then I have a good family, I have invested all my money. I really don't mind. I will be gutted for half an hour but on Tuesday I'll be in Tenerife.

articles.title: 'I deserve to be in!' - Spaun uses Team USA snub as fuel for Wentworth win
articles.summary: JJ Spaun said he played with a "huge chip on his shoulder" during his BMW PGA Championship win and used being snubbed by Team USA's Presidents Cup side as motivation for his Wentworth victory.
body: Spaun became the first player since Byeong Hun An in 2015 to win the DP World Tour's flagship event on debut, posting a final-round 67 to claim a two-shot success over Rory McIlroy, Aaron Rai, Adam Scott and Manuel Elvira.

Last year's US Open champion also won on the PGA Tour earlier this season at the Valero Texas Open and finished 10th in the Presidents Cup qualification standings, having also made his Team USA debut in the Ryder Cup last September.

Spaun was controversially overlooked for a captain's pick by Brandt Snedeker in his line-up to face the International Team in the biennial contest, live from Thursday on Sky Sports, with the 36-year-old pleased to respond by claiming a statement victory.
"The stars aligned this week for me to come out on top," Spaun said. "I'm just grateful to have the opportunity and play well and give myself a chance and came out with a W.
